Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 87
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 6912 of 2020
Applicant :- Smt Naziya
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Yogendra Pal Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as the learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The present bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 635 of 2020, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 504 I.P.C., Police Station Medical College, District Meerut.

entities.text: Police Station Medical College, District Meerut
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. As per the allegation in the FIR, the accused-applicant is a Service Provider and she has published an advertisement in newspaper for getting appointment in Hindi Call Centre.

In pursuance to the aforesaid advertisement, the complainant contacted the firm, J.T.M. Service New Krishna Plaza 05,
Jagriti Vihar, Heena Road Meerut and got registered himself there, for which she was paid Rs.
400/- and Rs. 800/-.
However, the complainant could not secure the job.

entities.text: Smt Naziya vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the accused-applicant submits that accused-applicant is an unmarried lady and, therefore, she is entitled to the protection of this Court by virtue of provisions contained in proviso to Section 437 Cr.P.C.

He further submits that the charging Sections alleged against the accused-applicant are 420, 467, 468, 471 and 504 I.P.C., but the accused-applicant has neither cheated the complainant nor prepared any document nor destroyed the whole or any part of a valuable security.

He also submits that F.I.R. was lodged on 20.8.2020, but the police has not collected any such material upto this stage, on the basis of which complicity of present accused-applicant can be said to be established.

He also submits that this Court after considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, granted interim protection to the accused-applicant on 19.10.2020 and she has cooperated during the course of investigation and she has not misused the liberty granted to her and, therefore, the accused-applicant may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
5. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail, but not disputed the aforesaid facts.
6. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds that the accused-applicant is entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
7. Accordingly, anticipatory bail application is allowed.

The accused-applicant is directed to appear before the trial court concerned within seven days from today and if she does so, she shall be released on anticipatory bail on her furnishing a personal bail bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, if already not filed, on the following conditions, which are imposed in the interest of justice, and other conditions, which may be desirable by the learned trial Court:-
(i) That the applicant shall make herself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;

(ii) That the applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer;
(iii) That the applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court; and (iv) Such other conditions as may be imposed under sub-section (3) of Section 437, as if the bail were granted under that section.
Order Date :- 21.2.2023 Rao/-
